refuted_findings.target_quote:
Set up cloud consoles that block headless automation (Google OAuth consent,
  Stripe webhooks, GCP credentials) by opening the exact URL in the local
  Windows Brave browser and handing paste-ready click steps, then wiring the
  reported credentials into Supabase/Vault/Vercel/.env. Use when a console step
  cannot be scripted: bot detection (Google's "browser may not be secure"), 2FA,
  CAPTCHA, or OAuth consent screens.
refuted_findings.issue: 'Google OAuth consent' (first parenthetical) and 'OAuth consent screens' (final clause) are the same branch named twice with different wording in the same always-loaded description. A run reaching the skill via either phrase takes the identical path (real-browser handoff, same playbook), so this pays the token cost of routing twice for one branch.
refuted_findings.proposed_fix: State the OAuth-consent trigger once, e.g. fold it into the closing list only: 'Use when a console step cannot be scripted: bot detection, 2FA, CAPTCHA, or OAuth consent screens (Google, Stripe, GCP).' and drop the separate 'Google OAuth consent' mention from the opening parenthetical.
refuted_findings.reason: panel 1/3 confirmed | REFUTED: The quoted text appears verbatim, but the rule doesn't genuinely apply — this is a single skill's description with one routing branch (frontmatter description → skill loads), not two separate branches; "Google OAuth consent" and "OAuth consent screens" are prose within the same always-loaded paragraph, not duplicate triggers causing redundant routing. || REFUTED — the quoted text is verbatim, but there's no branch structure here: the skill has a single path (real-browser handoff) and the two OAuth mentions serve different purposes (example use-case vs. trigger condition), not duplicate triggers for parallel branches. || CONFIRMED: The quoted text appears verbatim, and it does list "Google OAuth consent" and "OAuth consent screens" as separate phrasings for the same triggering condition within the always-loaded description.

refuted_findings.issue: "Clear" is a judgment term the agent cannot check without interpretation, unlike the other three checklist items which are binary (rules followed, identifiers included, commands ready). This stray uncheckable qualifier lets the agent tick the box impressionistically rather than verifying the concrete requirement the instruction template already defines ('Report back: [exactly what to copy back, with format]').
refuted_findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a checkable bound, e.g. '- [ ] "Report back" line specifies the exact value and format to copy (e.g. `whsec_...`)'.
